taylor: Heads up — saw sustained KV cache memory growth on a customer Private deployment while running long-context workloads (40k tokens). Hosted replica doesn't show the same growth; Dedicated shows intermittent fragmentation but stabilizes after GC. Not sure if this is config drift or an OS-level memalloc difference.

mona: repro steps? which model / sequence lengths?

taylor: repro script: send a 40k prompt split into 4k chunks with continuous attention; profile run for ~10k tokens of generation. Observed `kv_alloc` slowly climbing on Private box until paging occurs.

ash: do you have the runtime profile? any kernel selection differences?

leo: infra-bot attached basic profile (below) — looks like repeated `kv_page_alloc` + a lot of small free fragments (lots of holes).

infra-bot: ```
runtimectl profile --kv --output short
run_id: 2026-03-12-001
model: llama-70b
seq: 40960
kv_pages_total: 2912
kv_pages_active: 2789
kv_pages_free_fragments: 423
kv_page_size: 256KB
kv_alloc_bytes: 745MB -> 1.9GB (steady increase)
page_evictions: 112
page_reloads: 108
mem_alloc_backing: mmap_anonymous
kernel_path: avx2_opt (Hosted) vs avx512_opt (Private)
```

mona: interesting that kernel_path differs — could be autotuner picking avx512 on on-prem GPU hosts which changes allocation granularity? also page_size 256KB seems mismatched with host hugepage config.

ash: Dedicated runs on cloud VMs with 2MB hugepages enabled by default; Hosted infra uses 1GB hugetlbfs for inference. Private customer VMs we saw don't enable hugetlb by default which could cause fragmentation.

leo: Also saw sysctl vm.max_map_count differences; Private had default 65530, Dedicated bumped to 262144. That affects mmap fragmentation when we use many small kv frames.

ash: Proposed quick mitigations:
- align kv_page_size with host hugepage (detect & fallback)
- add compacting GC pass after X tokens to coalesce free fragments
- tune kernel selection to avoid allocations that increase fragmentation on avx512 path

mona: can we detect at startup: if hugetlb disabled -> set kv_page_size=2MB and enable coalescing? fallback to smaller pages if not supported.

ash: yes. patch prototype:
```
// pseudocode
if (!hugetlb_available()) kv_config.page_size = 2 * 1024 * 1024;
kv_config.compact_after_tokens = 8192;
kv_config.evict_threshold = 0.85;
```

leo: also need to account for VPC customers where tmpfs fallback may be mounted with small default_mtu causing larger page IO penalties. On Private deployments with strict VPC setups, we saw slower eviction -> more reloads.

infra-bot: deploy bot: canary rollout queued for eng-runtime/kv-compact (sha: a1b2c3) to dedicated clusters only.

mona: before rolling to Private, let's add a passive telemetry flag to capture `kv_free_fragments` + `hugetlb_state` on startup (opt-in for customers). then we can compare.

ash: agree. also need to check kernel selection: the avx512 implementation uses a different memory alignment for sparse KV frames; patch to align allocations to 2MB boundaries on avx512 seemed to reduce fragmentation in our lab runs.

taylor: lab result summary after alignment patch: 48h run with 40k seq -> kv_alloc plateaued at 1.1GB vs 1.9GB before; page_evictions dropped ~70%. no perf regression in p99 latency.

leo: follow-ups: open ticket INTERNAL-789 to track: 
- telemetry flag PR (mona)
- compacting GC implementation (ash)
- kernel alloc alignment change (ash)
- canary rollout plan to Private customers (leo)

taylor: thanks — i'll paste customer log snippets to the ticket.

mona: optional: consider making `kv_compact` a periodic background job rather than synchronous GC to avoid tail latency spikes.

ash: noted. We'll prototype background compaction.

leo: tagging folks for visibility: @mona @ash @taylor. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: scheduled canary: eng-runtime/kv-compact -> dedicated-us-east-1 at 2026-03-15T09:00Z

taylor: cool, i'll keep notes in the ticket and grab traces from the Private customer once they opt in.

leo: small note — Dedicated vs Hosted cost/perf tradeoff: Hosted can use SSD-backed paging with predictable throughput; Dedicated relies on local ephemeral NVMe and is sensitive to kernel tunables; Private vary widely. Keep rollout conservative.

ash: agreed. TL;DR: fragmentation + missing hugetlb + kernel alloc alignment differences explain the growth on Private. Plan: telemetry -> canary compact GC on Dedicated -> verify improvement -> private opt-in rollout.
